newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs steady-off $0.50 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs steady-off $0.50 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Monday sold mostly steady, instances $0.50 per cwt lower, in light activity, livestock dealers said.
Weakness was tied to soft demand from packers who already had live inventories lined up from hogs booked late last week, the dealers said.
However, those packers still needing hogs paid steady prices because of light marketings early Monday, they said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs mostly sold $0.50 lower at $54.50 to $55.00 in the country and $55.50 to $57.00 at plants, dealers and packer buyers there said.
Illinois hogs sold steady at $54.50 to $55.50 in the country and $56.00 to $56.50 at plants, with a possible $57.00, sources there said.
Indiana hogs sold steady in slow activity, with $55.00 to $55.50 paid in the country and $56.00 to $57.00 at plants.
Ohio hogs also sold steady at $55.50 to $56.00 in the country and $56.50 to $57.00 at plants, sources said.
Hog numbers were seen gradually increasing into the winter, which could slowly erode prices the next few months unless retail or export pork demand picks up, several market sources said.
